info.title: Quak API
info.description:
The Quak API plays announcements on Sonos speakers: text-to-speech, sounds, own clips, files, URLs and push-to-talk, with voice effects and ambiences, quiet hours and a live history.

## Authentication

To get an API key:

1. Call `POST /v1/user/signup` (new account) or `POST /v1/user/login` with your email address.

2. Confirm the request via the email link.

3. Exchange the `verifyToken` using `POST /v1/user/login/key` to receive your API key.

Use the API key on protected endpoints with either:

- Header: `Authorization: Bearer <API_KEY>` (raw token also works). Recommended.

- Query parameter: `?apikey=<API_KEY>`, handy for demos and quick tests. A key in a URL can end up in logs, the browser history and referrers of the tools on the way, so use the header in integrations.

API keys look like `qk_key_…` (43 characters). The full key is shown once, when it is made (`POST /v1/keys`, `POST /v1/user/login/key`); Quak only keeps a hash of it. Lists show its start (`qk_key_7Fh2…`).

## Workspaces, roles and scopes

A workspace holds the credits and subscription, the Sonos accounts and speakers, groups, clips, keys and the playback defaults (`GET /v1/workspace`). Every user gets a personal workspace at sign-up and can be a member of more (`GET /v1/workspaces`, invitations with `POST /v1/workspace/invites`); plays keep who triggered them.

Which workspace a request works in: a **login key** (from logging in with an app, the website or the CLI) belongs to you, not to a workspace. Name the workspace per request with the header `X-Quak-Workspace: <slug or id>`; without it the request works in the workspace you named last, else your personal one. Switching needs no new login. A key made with `POST /v1/keys` belongs to one workspace; a header naming another one is `403 ERROR_WORKSPACE_MISMATCH`. The workspace of a request is in the `X-Quak-Workspace-UUID` header of the answer.

Both have to allow a request: the key's **scope** and your **role** in the workspace. Scopes include the ones below: `play` (read speakers, voices, sounds, credits, history and play, costs credits) < `create` (and add clips: upload one or keep a play as one) < `manage` (and settings, Sonos accounts, keys, groups, renaming and deleting clips, members). Keys made with `POST /v1/keys` get `play` unless asked otherwise, login keys `manage`. Roles: `MEMBER` reads and plays (and adds clips); `ADMIN` also runs the workspace, several admins are equal. Changing the email and creating workspaces need a login key. Every endpoint names its scope; with too little the answer is `403 ERROR_INSUFFICIENT_SCOPE`, with a role too low `403 ERROR_INSUFFICIENT_ROLE`, both with the need in `details.required`.

## Identifiers

- `id`: stable UUID identifier exposed in public API payloads.

- `slug`: human-friendly identifier on slug-enabled resources (for example Sonos accounts).

For slug-enabled resources, `/{id}` path params can accept either `id` or `slug`.

## Playback

Play text (`POST /v1/play/text`), built-in sounds, own clips, URLs, uploaded files and what someone said into a mic (`POST /v1/play/talk` after release, `GET /v1/play/talk/live` as a WebSocket while talking) on your Sonos speakers. Missing parameters come from the workspace defaults (`PATCH /v1/workspace/defaults`), including quiet hours (default `22-7`, in the workspace time zone): a play during quiet hours is not played, costs nothing and returns `200` with status `SKIPPED`. `preview: true` only produces the audio and returns its `audioUrl`. Every play is kept in the history (`GET /v1/plays`) and can be stopped while it runs.

Credits: 1 when Sonos fetches from the CDN or the source (sound, clip, URL without processing), 2 when the audio goes through the API server (TTS, processed URL, file, talk), plus the voice rate per started 100 characters for TTS and 1 per started 10 s of speech for talk. A TTS cache hit (same text and voice within the workspace's audio cache time, `PATCH /v1/workspace/audio-cache`) costs 2, the preview skips the base fee. The balance after the play is in the `X-Quak-Credits` header.

## Audio formats

Everything Quak plays is mono, a Sonos room plays on one speaker (a stereo pair only on the left one), so mono uploads lose nothing.

- **Uploads** (`POST /v1/play/file`, `POST /v1/play/talk`, `POST /v1/clips`): any common audio format, for example MP3, M4A/AAC, Opus (WebM or Ogg), WAV or FLAC, max. 10 MB and 180 s. Prefer a compressed format (MP3, M4A, Opus): a WAV of 180 s is about 15 MB mono and does not fit, an MP3 at 128 kbit/s is about 3 MB. For talk the browser's `MediaRecorder` output (WebM/Opus) or iOS M4A can be sent as is.

- **URLs with processing** (`POST /v1/play/url`, default): like uploads, the server downloads and converts them.

- **URLs without processing** (`process: false`): Sonos fetches the file itself, so it must be **MP3** (or WAV) on a public HTTPS URL. Use MP3: Sonos does not play WAV files shorter than about one second.

- **What Sonos gets** from Quak is MP3 (128 kbit/s, 44.1 kHz, mono) for generated audio, sounds and clips.

## Responses

The API can return these status codes across endpoints:

- `200 OK`: request succeeded.

- `201 Created`: a resource was created (for example an API key).

- `202 Accepted`: request is valid but completion is still pending (for example login confirmation wait mode).

- `204 No Content`: request succeeded and no response body is returned (typically delete endpoints).

- `302 Found`: redirect response (for example Sonos connect with `redirect=1`).

- `400 Bad Request`: invalid query/body/path parameters.

- `401 Unauthorized`: API key missing, invalid or deleted (log in again), or an expired/invalid login verify token.

- `402 Payment Required`: not enough credits for the play.

- `403 Forbidden`: the API key is valid but may not do this.

- `404 Not Found`: requested resource does not exist in your scope.

- `409 Conflict`: uniqueness conflict (for example duplicate API key name) or a play that is not running any more.

- `422 Unprocessable Content`: request body failed schema validation.

- `424 Failed Dependency`: no speaker accepted the play (for example offline or gone), or Sonos did not let it stop.

- `503 Service Unavailable`: a service behind Quak failed, for example Sonos or the speech synthesis. Quak never answers with 502 or 504.

Scope: `play`. Returns the available voices of AWS Polly, Google (Chirp 3 HD and Gemini), OpenAI and ElevenLabs, see `provider` and `model`. Pass a voice `slug` as `voice` to POST /v1/play/text. Optional filter for multi-language voices: true returns only voices that speak every language of their model, false only single-language voices.

Optional CSV language filter (case-insensitive OR match). Multi-language voices match every language their model supports. Sorted by latency (fast, normal, slow), within each class voices whose own language matches first. `mul` returns the multi-language voices without a native language. Example: de,en

post.description: Scope: `play`. Plays what someone said into a mic, after release. Unlike play/file the audio runs through the voice processing (high-pass, noise gate, auto gain, a fixed EQ), silence at start and end is cut and at most 180 s (3 minutes) of speech are played. get.description:
**WebSocket.** Connect to `wss://<host>/v1/play/talk/live` (a GET with `Upgrade: websocket`), not a plain HTTP request. The protocol is below.

Beta, may change without notice. Plays what someone says while they say it. Start with the first message {"type":"start","apiKey":"…","to":…,"volume":…,"volumes":{…},"effect":…,"effectIntensity":…,"ambience":…,"ambienceIntensity":…,"intro":…,"outro":…,"gap":…,"priority":…,"quietHours":…,"format":{"encoding":"opus"|"pcm_s16le"|"pcm_f32le","sampleRate":16000|24000|44100|48000}} (or the Authorization header). From a browser that should not see the key: "ticket":"qk_wst_…" instead of "apiKey", a one-time ticket from POST /v1/ws/tickets with purpose talk-live (60 s, it names the workspace; an invalid one closes with 4401 and ERROR_INVALID_TICKET). Browsers from other origins are refused (4403). The answer is {"type":"ready","play":{…}}, then send the audio as binary frames (Opus: one raw 20 ms packet per frame; PCM: mono, little endian). While talking: {"type":"update","effect":…,"effectIntensity":…,"ambience":…,"ambienceIntensity":…,"muted":…} → {"type":"updated",…}. End with {"type":"end"} → {"type":"done","play":{…},"credits":…,"balance":…} (balance: the workspace's credits after the charge). At most 3 minutes, a warning comes 30 s before. Faster, slower and reverse do not work live. Errors: {"type":"error","code","message","field","requestId"} and the socket closes with 4000 + the HTTP status. Credits: 2 at the start (with credits for a minute of speech), 1 per started 10 s of speech after the end.

post.description: Scope: `play`. Plays one of your clips from /v1/clips, fetched by Sonos from the CDN. Played as stored unless process: true; a processing field alone (intro, outro, gap, effect, ambience) does not turn processing on and is ignored. With process: true it gets intro, outro, gap, effect and ambience from the workspace defaults, fields of the request override them and none turns one off, mixed on the server and cached. Credits: 1, processed 2.

process.description: true: intro, outro, gap, effect and ambience like a processed URL, mixed on the server and cached (2 credits). The account defaults (intro, outro, gap, effect, ambience) apply, fields in the request override them, none turns one off. Default false: played as stored, Sonos fetches it from the CDN (1 credit), processing fields are ignored

gap.description: pause between intro, content and outro in ms: 0, 100, ..., 1000, default: the user default

effectIntensity.description: Beta, may change without notice. strength of the voice effect, default: the user default (medium), off = no effect. What each level means is tuned per effect.

ambience.description: Beta, may change without notice. place behind the voice, combinable with effect, default: the workspace default (sounds and clips only with process: true)

ambienceIntensity.description: Beta, may change without notice. level of the ambience, default: the user default (medium), off = no ambience

get.description:
**WebSocket.** Connect to `wss://<host>/v1/plays/watch` (a GET with `Upgrade: websocket`), not a plain HTTP request. The protocol is below.

Live status of your plays. Log in with the first message {"type":"auth","apiKey":"…"} (or the Authorization header). From a browser that should not see the key: {"type":"auth","ticket":"qk_wst_…"} or ?ticket=, a one-time ticket from POST /v1/ws/tickets with purpose watch (60 s, an invalid one closes with 4401 and ERROR_INVALID_TICKET). Browsers from other origins are refused (4403). A login key watches the workspace named by `workspace` in that message, ?workspace= or X-Quak-Workspace (slug or id), else the last used one. Then you get {"type":"ready"}, every running play once and every change of a play as {"type":"play","data":{…}} (the same object as GET /v1/plays/:uuid), plus {"type":"ping"} every 25 s. Reconnect after a drop, you get the current state again.

Keeps the audio of a play as one of your clips, exactly as it played (intro, outro and effect included), to play it again with POST /v1/play/clip or use it as intro or outro. post.description: Scope: `play`. Plays the audio of a play once more, exactly as it played (intro, outro and effect included), e.g. what someone said into the mic, a preview on the speakers, or again in another room. Speakers, volume, volumes, priority and quiet hours are the ones of the play unless the body names others; the content cannot change (for another effect play it again, a text reuses its speech). A new play in the history with params.replayOf. Works for sounds and clips, and for text, talk, file and processed url plays while their audio is there (the audio cache time), else 409 ERROR_AUDIO_GONE. Not for talk live and url plays without processing (400 ERROR_NOT_REPLAYABLE). Credits: only the base fee, 1 for sounds and clips, 2 for the rest.
